items.title: AI-enabled genomic pattern discovery in Epstein-Barr virus on Amazon EC2
items.summary: This post, which details a collaboration between a national genomics research institute and Temus using Amazon Web Services (AWS), demonstrates the power of combining deep bioinformatics with advanced AI models and machine learning methods in a scalable AWS environment to uncover novel patterns in complex viral genomes. In this post, we explore the details of a scalable proof of concept (POC) pipeline built on AWS that uses an advanced genomic foundation model and unsupervised clustering to transform raw genomic sequences into signals for further research.

items.title: Practical digital sovereignty: Building a sovereign landing zone on AWS
items.summary: In this post, we translate pillars into a deployable cloud foundation, focusing on the key postures of security, identity management, governance, network design, resilience, continuity, auditability, and operational independence.

items.title: AI as force multiplier: Practical AI governance for HCLS security teams
items.summary: AI handles triage while analysts handle judgment. And, by coupling automated continuous monitoring with AI system connectivity, recovery time can speed up, resulting in fewer after-hours status calls. Your existing Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment already has access to the capabilities that can make this a reality.

items.title: Amazon Cognito extends multi-Region replication to AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
items.summary: Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication (MRR) now supports AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, extending the resilience benefits of MRR to more workloads. MRR lets you synchronize user and machine identity data, including credentials, user pool configurations, and federation setups, to a secondary user pool in a standby Region you designate, in near real-time. With user data in the standby Region, you can redirect traffic and keep authentication available if there is a disruption in your primary Region. items.title: How Proscia built unlimited observability with Amazon S3 and the Altinity Kubernetes Operator
items.summary: Observability can claim a growing share of IT budgets. Learn how Proscia, a pathology AI company, built a self-hosted observability platform on Amazon S3, Amazon EKS, and ClickHouse managed by the Altinity Kubernetes Operator, achieving unlimited telemetry retention at object-storage cost under HIPAA, GDPR, and data-residency requirements.

items.title: Updating encryption on existing Amazon S3 objects with S3 Batch Operations
items.summary: Large organizations accumulate billions of Amazon S3 objects under different encryption configurations. Learn how to use S3 Batch Operations with the new UpdateObjectEncryption API to standardize encryption across an entire bucket at scale. The approach moves objects from SSE-S3 to SSE-KMS in place, with no data movement and without breaking S3 Lifecycle policies.

With your access logs in CloudWatch Logs, you can query them as they arrive, set alarms, and encrypt them with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys. This new delivery path complements the existing delivery of server access logs to S3 general purpose buckets, giving you more flexibility in how you monitor and analyze access to your data. items.title: AWS Network Firewall now supports Route 53 Resolved IP Validation

This feature enables Network Firewall customers to implement domain filtering rules for any protocol, not just HTTP/HTTPS, providing more flexible security policies than IP-based rules alone. Whichever path you choose, you arrive on AWS with a secure and scalable network foundation.
